html:
Elite troops who guarded the emperors of Rome, from their creation by augustus about 27 BCE until Constantine disbanded them in 312 CE.

Augustus set up nine cohorts of about 500 men and kept them close to Rome, which was unusual, since armies were barred from the city. They got double pay and short service. Under tiberius the guard prefect Sejanus nearly ruled the state.

Because they stood nearest the emperor, they could also remove him. In 41 CE they helped kill Caligula and then found claudius and made him emperor, expecting a reward. In 68 they dropped nero. In 193 they murdered Pertinax and sold the throne to the highest bidder, in the Year of the Five Emperors.

Septimius Severus punished them and rebuilt the guard with his own legionaries. In 312 Constantine beat their candidate, Maxentius, and abolished the guard.
sum: Elite troops who guarded the emperors of Rome, from their creation by augustus about 27 BCE until Constantine disbanded them in 312 CE.
